name: a-grip-drag-on-a-realistic-page-keeps-the-sidebar-drawing
description:
The third page weight for the same 80pt 40-step grip drag. The light sibling loads a short page and the heavy one 3000 bare paragraphs; neither is what a user browses. This fixture is 300 paragraphs plus 60 flex/grid containers of 360 boxes, with a resize listener that reads offsetWidth back on every resize, so each resize message costs a real synchronous style-and-layout flush the way a responsive site does.

It records the pane side (widths-seen, worst-gap) and the page side (steps, settle, quiet) from one drag, so a change that buys pane tracking by handing the page a backlog cannot read as a win here.

Numbers only, no threshold: one picked before the first reading is a guess.

actions.expression: (() => { window.__drag = {frames: [], rebuilds: 0, longtasks: []}; const root = document.getElementById('atrium-root'); window.__dragObs = new MutationObserver((records) => { for (const r of records) { if (r.target === root) { window.__drag.rebuilds++; } } }); window.__dragObs.observe(root, {childList: true}); try { window.__dragPerf = new PerformanceObserver((list) => { for (const e of list.getEntries()) { window.__drag.longtasks.push([Math.round(e.startTime), Math.round(e.duration), e.name]); } }); window.__dragPerf.observe({entryTypes: ['longtask']}); } catch (e) { window.__drag.longtasks.push([-1, -1, 'unsupported: ' + e.name]); } const tick = (t) => { window.__drag.frames.push([Math.round(t), document.documentElement.clientWidth]); window.__dragRaf = requestAnimationFrame(tick); }; window.__dragRaf = requestAnimationFrame(tick); return 'armed'; })()
actions.note: armed before the drag, so no frame of it is skipped
the wall clock the last pointer step landed at - every page step after this is tail
ASSERTED here, unlike the 3000-paragraph rig: on a page of this weight the reflows really do stop inside the window, so a backlog fails it.
THE CONTROL for every reading below: a sampler that never ran reports no gaps at all
THE PRESENCE CONTROL: one width means the drag never reached the pane, so the frame reading is of a still sidebar

actions.expression: (() => { const seen = new Set(window.__drag.frames.map((f) => f[1])).size; return seen >= 25 ? 'tracks' : 'stepped, only ' + seen + ' widths for 40 pointer steps'; })()
actions.note: Recorded not asserted. The sibling heavy-page rig reports 9-11 widths for 40 steps. A number well above that here means the stutter belongs to the page's layout cost, not to the grip.

actions.expression: (() => { const f = window.__drag.frames; let worst = 0; for (let i = 1; i < f.length; i++) { worst = Math.max(worst, f[i][0] - f[i - 1][0]); } return String(worst); })()
actions.note: The longest the sidebar went without drawing, in ms

actions.expression: (() => { const f = window.__drag.frames; let slow = 0; for (let i = 1; i < f.length; i++) { if (f[i][0] - f[i - 1][0] > 20) { slow++; } } return String(slow); })()
actions.note: How many frames took longer than one 60Hz interval

actions.expression: (() => { const f = window.__drag.frames; let last = 0; for (let i = 1; i < f.length; i++) { if (f[i][1] !== f[i - 1][1]) { last = i; } } let worst = 0; for (let i = 1; i <= last; i++) { worst = Math.max(worst, f[i][0] - f[i - 1][0]); } return String(worst); })()
actions.note: The longest gap up to the last width change, which is the drag itself. A release that costs one reflow lands after this and cannot inflate it

actions.expression: (() => { const f = window.__drag.frames; let last = 0; for (let i = 1; i < f.length; i++) { if (f[i][1] !== f[i - 1][1]) { last = i; } } let worst = 0; for (let i = last + 1; i < f.length; i++) { worst = Math.max(worst, f[i][0] - f[i - 1][0]); } return String(worst); })()
actions.note: the release's own cost: fast resize defers the page's reflow to here, so one gap is expected and is the trade being made
Attribution for the gaps above: what the renderer was busy with, and for how long
Whole-DOM rebuilds of #atrium-root paid for during the drag
THE CONTROL for the fixture: zero means the resize listener never ran, so this page cost no more than the short one

assertions.desc: the per-frame sampler was installed before the drag, not after it
